stories.headline: Khamenei issues "final ultimatum" to Pezeshkian, backs IRGC commander
stories.body: Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei warned President Pezeshkian that any future resignation would be accepted, and threw his support behind IRGC commander Ahmad Vahidi on key negotiation and conflict decisions. The move sidelines Pezeshkian from strategic decision-making and aligns the regime fully with its military establishment. Trump called Iranian leadership "unbelievably duplicitous" after Tehran denied talks had resumed.

stories.headline: Oil crashes below $84 as Trump's Iran pause triggers biggest drop in weeks
stories.body: Brent fell ~5% to below $84/barrel; WTI dropped below $80. Oil had surged 20%+ in July, peaking near $126 at the height of the conflict. Exxon Mobil doubled Q2 profits to $14.53B (+105% YoY); Chevron nearly quadrupled to $12.07B (+385% YoY) on the war-driven price spike.
stories.sources: NYT, Trading Economics, Yahoo Finance, CNBC

stories.headline: Gaza: 1,230+ killed since October ceasefire as Israel continues strikes
stories.body: Israeli drone and air strikes killed at least 16 Palestinians on Sunday. An estimated 1,230 have died since the October ceasefire. Israel formally challenges the disarmament roadmap's sequencing. Hamas agreed to hand weapons to a committee of Egypt, Qatar, and Turkey mediators. The UAE welcomed it as a "major step."

stories.headline: Kumamoto recovery accelerates but 40°C heat creates secondary death crisis
stories.body: One week post-quake, death toll at 38. A woman in her 70s died of heatstroke while sheltering in her car. 9,200+ in 210 evacuation centers. Focus shifted from rescue to heat-risk management as temperatures exceed 40°C.
stories.sources: Nikkei Asia, NHK World, Japan Times

stories.headline: SpaceX reports first-ever earnings; $116B lock-up expiry looms
stories.body: SpaceX (SPCX) releases its first quarterly results after market close. The report triggers a major insider lock-up expiration — $116B in shares could hit the market. Trading at ~49x expected revenue. Wall Street focused on Starship progress, Starlink revenue, and launch cadence.

take: The Khamenei ultimatum is the most important story of the day — it effectively kills the peace talks before they start. Oil at $84 is a relief rally built on sand. Gaza at 1,230 killed since the October ceasefire should make everyone stop using the word ceasefire. Kumamoto's shift from rescue to heat-risk management is where death tolls creep up silently. SpaceX's first earnings is the financial event of the week — 49x revenue prices in Mars colonization.

stories.headline: Trump calls off "biggest attack since WWII" on Iran, says talks resume Monday
stories.body: President Trump announced he canceled a massive planned strike on Iran — described as potentially the largest since World War II — at the request of Gulf allies. He claimed a deal on the Strait of Hormuz is "imminent." However, Iran denied requesting Trump call off the strikes.
stories.sources: CNN, CBS News, NBC News, ABC News

stories.headline: Israel kills 19 in Gaza as strikes continue despite disarmament plan
stories.body: Israeli airstrikes hit Gaza for a second straight day, killing at least 19 Palestinians. An Israeli minister said there is "no deal" to halt attacks. Israel has formally raised concerns with the US over the proposed disarmament roadmap, challenging key provisions linking Hamas disarmament to phased Israeli withdrawal.

stories.headline: Indonesian ferry fire: 5 dead, 41 missing off Madura Island
stories.body: A passenger ferry carrying 271 people caught fire in waters off Madura Island, East Java. At least 5 confirmed dead, 41 unaccounted for. Rescue teams are searching for survivors. Maritime accidents are common in Indonesia, where safety regulations are inconsistently enforced.

stories.headline: Brazil's PT nominates Lula for unprecedented fourth term
stories.body: The Workers' Party officially nominated President Lula da Silva as its candidate for the 2026 election at a convention in São Paulo. Geraldo Alckmin confirmed as running mate. Lula, 80, seeks an unprecedented fourth term. Polls show a tight race against a Bolsonaro-aligned right.

stories.headline: Kumamoto quake death toll hits 38 as survivors battle extreme heat
stories.body: Death toll from the magnitude 7.1 earthquake has risen to at least 38. More than 9,200 people remain in 210 evacuation centers. 3,851 homes damaged. Survivors are battling intense heat — heat-related illnesses are now a secondary crisis on top of the earthquake damage.
stories.sources: Japan Times, Al Jazeera, Nikkei Asia

take: Trump calling off the Iran strike is the most significant de-escalation signal in months — but the gap between his rhetoric and reality is enormous. Iran says they never asked him to pause. Gaza is the contradiction at the heart of Trump's peace diplomacy. Lula running for a fourth term at 80 is a test of whether Brazil's left can hold power. Kumamoto's shift from rescue to heat-risk management is where death tolls creep up silently.

stories.headline: Nims Purja confirmed dead — body recovered from Broad Peak
stories.body: Pakistani officials confirmed the body of Nirmal "Nims" Purja was recovered from Broad Peak (8,047m). All 10 climbers caught in Thursday's avalanche have been recovered or located. Purja, 43, held the record for fastest ascent of all 14 eight-thousanders (6 months, 6 days) and completed the first winter ascent of K2 in 2021.
stories.sources: Al Jazeera, ABC News, NYT, Climbing.com

stories.headline: Ceuta border crisis: death toll reaches 67
stories.body: The Spanish government confirmed 67 people have died in the Ceuta-Morocco border crisis. Victims drowned or were killed in a stampede to cross a breakwater barrier. Tens of thousands of migrants crossed into the Spanish enclave this week. Spanish PM Sánchez denounced the "selfish" response of EU member states.

stories.headline: Iran war: US prepares expanded bombardment as Hormuz escorts paused
stories.body: US Central Command has prepared options for a heavy 2-week bombardment of Iran's missile sites. The UN International Maritime Organization paused its escort operation through the Strait of Hormuz after a vessel reported an attack. Iran warned it has a "retaliation plan ready." Oil remains near $110/barrel.

stories.headline: Apple & Amazon beat earnings; Tim Cook's last call as CEO
stories.body: Apple Q3: $109.4B revenue (+16% YoY), EPS $2.02 (+29%), but services revenue missed. Amazon beat on both sales and profits (+7% after-hours). This was Tim Cook's final earnings call as CEO. The BOJ separately held rates at 1% (8-1 vote), warning core inflation will exceed its 2% target.

stories.headline: South Carolina GOP primary Aug. 11 to replace Lindsey Graham
stories.body: A special Republican primary on August 11 will determine who replaces the late Sen. Lindsey Graham on the November ballot. Graham's sister, state Sen. Darline Graham, is among the candidates. The Democratic nominee is pediatrician Annie Andrews. The race is being watched as a MAGA vs. establishment proxy war.

take: Nims Purja's death is the end of an era. The man who did the impossible died on a mountain other teams had already evacuated. Ceuta at 67 dead is being underreported — past crisis management into structural failure. The Iran war is entering its most dangerous phase. Mag 7 earnings are decoupling from macro economy via AI capex, but Apple's services miss signals installed-base saturation.

stories.headline: Hamas disarmament conditions emerge
stories.body: Detailed conditions for the disarmament roadmap emerge. Hamas must hand weapons to a committee of Egypt, Qatar, and Turkey mediators. Israel formally challenges the sequencing — disarmament first vs. withdrawal first. The deal's text remains unpublished.

stories.headline: Kumamoto earthquake recovery: death toll at 20
stories.body: Death toll rises to 20. 7,000+ in shelters. Heat wave compounds rescue efforts. Infrastructure damage assessed at ¥800B+. Shinkansen service partially restored. Thousands still without power and water in rural areas.

stories.headline: Iran war escalation: Hormuz shipping traffic drops 40%
stories.body: IRGC continues strikes on Gulf state energy infrastructure. Strait of Hormuz shipping traffic drops 40%. Insurance rates for tankers spike 300%. CENTCOM deploys additional Patriot batteries to the region.

stories.headline: US economy: Q2 GDP grows at 1.5%, Fed signals no rate cut
stories.body: Q2 GDP grows at 1.5%, below expectations. Fed signals no rate cut in 2026. Stagflation fears intensify as inflation remains sticky while growth decelerates. Consumer spending weakens.

stories.headline: EU migration crisis: Ceuta prompts emergency summit
stories.body: Ceuta border crisis prompts emergency EU summit. Frontex deploys additional border guards. Spain demands more solidarity from Brussels as tens of thousands cross from Morocco in a single week.

take: The Hamas deal's sequencing dispute is the core problem. Israel won't withdraw without genuine disarmament; Hamas won't disarm while Israel occupies. The detailed conditions document is due in 2 weeks — if it doesn't solve sequencing with ironclad third-party enforcement, this deal is dead by September. The GDP number confirms stagflation: growth slowing, inflation sticky, no rate cuts coming.

stories.headline: Trump announces Hamas disarmament deal
stories.body: President Trump announced a roadmap for Hamas to disarm in exchange for phased Israeli withdrawal from Gaza. Details remain sparse. The deal was brokered with Egypt, Qatar, and Turkey as mediators.

stories.headline: Iran strikes Gulf allies
stories.body: IRGC missile strikes hit energy infrastructure in Saudi Arabia, UAE, and Qatar. Oil surges past $110/barrel. CENTCOM deploys additional Patriot batteries. The strikes mark a shift from proxy warfare to direct state-on-state escalation.

stories.headline: Nims Purja missing on Broad Peak
stories.body: Legendary mountaineer Nirmal "Nims" Purja reported missing on Broad Peak (8,047m). Rescue teams dispatched. Purja held the record for fastest ascent of all 14 eight-thousanders. An avalanche hit the mountain during a summit push.

stories.headline: Meta faces regulatory pressure in India
stories.body: Meta faces regulatory pressure in India over WhatsApp privacy changes. New data localization rules take effect. The Indian government threatens fines for non-compliance with IT Act amendments.
stories.sources: Reuters, Times of India, Economic Times

stories.headline: Kumamoto earthquake: death toll rises to 12
stories.body: Death toll rises to 12. 5,000+ in shelters. Shinkansen service partially restored. Tsunami advisory lifted. Nuclear regulator confirms Sendai nuclear plant safe.

take: Trump's Hamas disarmament deal is ambitious but the sequencing problem — disarmament first or withdrawal first — is the same trap that killed every previous deal. The Iran strikes on Gulf states mark a new phase: this is no longer proxy warfare, it's direct state-on-state escalation. Nims Purja missing is a gut punch for the climbing world.

stories.headline: Magnitude 7.1 earthquake strikes Kumamoto, Japan
stories.body: A magnitude 7.1 earthquake struck the Kumamoto region. Multiple buildings collapsed, tsunami advisory issued. Nuclear regulator monitoring Sendai nuclear plant. Shinkansen service suspended for safety inspection.

stories.headline: US-Saudi joint strikes on Iran-backed militias
stories.body: Joint military operation targets Houthi and Hezbollah positions. Pentagon says strikes are a "proportional response" to Red Sea shipping attacks. The operation involved both airstrikes and naval bombardment.

stories.headline: Telegram founder Pavel Durov formally charged
stories.body: Durov formally charged by French authorities for failure to moderate content. Released on €5M bail. The charges set a precedent for platform liability that could reshape European tech regulation.

stories.headline: BMW announces 8,000 job cuts in Germany
stories.body: BMW announces 8,000 job cuts in Germany as EV transition accelerates. Union threatens strikes. The cuts represent one of the largest single layoffs in the German auto industry's transition era.

take: The Japan quake is the immediate humanitarian story, but the US-Saudi strikes signal a dangerous escalation. Durov's charges set a precedent for platform liability that could reshape European tech. BMW's cuts are the canary in the coal mine for legacy auto — the EV transition isn't just about batteries, it's about labor.
